payload.name: Redundancy Effect
payload.fact: Redundant information presented through multiple channels (e.g., simultaneous on-screen text and narration, or duplicated modal information) tends to decrease learning outcomes and increase cognitive load, but findings are contested, with some studies reporting no significant redundancy effect or context-dependent benefits.
payload.boundary: Applies to modality-based redundancy in multimedia learning materials, distinguished from content redundancy; direction and magnitude of the effect vary across studies and instructional contexts, and some research finds no significant impact on learning or cognitive load.

provenance.title: A redundant redundancy principle? examining the redundancy principle through cognitive load
provenance.quote_or_locus: Results indicate that there was no evidence of a significant redundancy effect for learning. Furthermore, measures of cognitive load showed no significant differences between the three conditions

provenance.title: Redundancy effect in multimedia learning
provenance.quote_or_locus: That is the reverse redundancy effect is true for multimedia learning of English as a foreign language for students where textual information was foreign to them. In such situations, the redundant synchronized on-screen text did not impede learning; rather it reduced the cognitive load and thereby enhanced learning

provenance.title: The Redundancy Effect on Retention and Transfer for Individuals with High Symptoms of ADHD
provenance.quote_or_locus: Individuals with higher-reported ADHD symptoms had lower performance levels when using the multimedia presentation with redundancy

provenance.title: Evaluation of redundancy effect in multimedia learning environment using EEG signals and eye-tracking
provenance.quote_or_locus: The findings suggested that the redundancy group demonstrated elevated cognitive load, especially in the frontal and parietal regions

provenance.title: Cognitive constraints on multimedia learning: When presenting more material results in less understanding.
provenance.quote_or_locus: When students also received concurrent on-screen text that summarized (Experiment 1) or duplicated (Experiment 2) the narration, they performed worse on tests of retention and transfer than did students who received no on-screen text

provenance.title: Different types of redundancy and their effect on learning and cognitive load
provenance.quote_or_locus: while modal redundancy decreases learning outcomes and increases cognitive load

provenance.title: Readdressing the Redundancy Effect: a Cognitive Strategy for E-learning Design
provenance.quote_or_locus: Results indicate that the Redundancy mode is most effective for learning, that is, the simultaneous presentation of text and narration enables significantly more optimal learning
